title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
abstract: arXiv:2611.30637v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames. For six models, the success rate peaks at intermediate speeds, and their failures indicate that they tend to produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed rather than to the actual one. Past frames raise the success rate by 10-40

translated_title: SWEEP-Bench：具身策略能否按其所见的速度行动？
translated_abstract: 机器人策略必须适应移动物体的速度，然而现有的基准测试很少能在多样化任务和速度范围内衡量这一能力。我们提出了SWEEP-Bench，这是一个包含80个传送带操作任务的仿真基准，涵盖16个技能类别，每个任务在13种传送带速度（0.10-0.40 m/s）下进行评估。物体通过与可见移动传送带的物理接触被运送。每个任务都有一个对应的静态版本，并且每次评估回合在所有13种速度下使用相同的随机场景。我们在覆盖全速度范围的演示数据上对八个视觉-语言-动作模型和世界-动作模型进行微调，比较仅使用当前帧的观测与包含两个过去帧的观测。对于其中六个模型，成功率在中间速度时达到峰值，其失败情况表明它们倾向于产生适合演示平均速度而非实际速度的动作。引入过去帧能将成功率提高10-40个百分点。
tldr: 提出SWEEP-Bench仿真基准，通过80个传送带操作任务在13种速度下系统评估机器人策略对移动物体速度的适应能力，发现多数模型倾向于按演示平均速度而非实际速度行动，而加入历史帧信息可将成功率提升10-40个百分点。
en_tdlr: SWEEP-Bench is a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks evaluated across 13 belt speeds, revealing that most vision-language-action models produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed rather than the actual object speed, while incorporating past frames improves success rates by 10-40 percentage points.
